newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Norilsk says gas leak not to hit net output.
newsitem.headline: Russia Norilsk says gas leak not to hit net output.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel said that a natural gas line at its flagship enterprise leaked on Friday, but a spokesman said there would be no net effect on nickel output or exports targeted in the company's 1996 schedules.

"There will be no net loss of output, and there was no serious influence on the output of nickel," Sergei Vetchinin said, adding that the enterprise had reserves and would increase production if any losses were incurred.
He declined to be more specific or give details.
When asked if exports would be affected, he said, "No."

He said work at unspecified units of the enterprise's headquarters slowed down on Friday after a pipeline burst at 0800 hours local time, but that the situation was under control and the line would be reparied by 1600 hours.
Other pipelines had kept factories supplied with enough gas to avoid a stop in production, he said.

Vetchinin also said a trade union leader at the Dudinka port had threatened a strike over unpaid wages but that the situation was far from becoming a strike and Norilsk management would travel to the enterprise on Saturday for discussions.
"Valery Melnikov, one of the deputy leaders (of the port workers' union), said that if back wages were not paid, the port would strike," he said.
Dudinka is one of Norilsk's export outlets.
RAO Norilskyz Nikel NKEL.RTS has reduced the back pay it owes most workers to two months' from four months' arrears, but port workers' wages were still four months overdue, Vetchinin said.
He said Norilsk chairman Alexander Khloponin would lead the Norilsk delegation to meet union leaders, but that the visit been scheduled in advance of the threatened strike.
"The situation is under control. We cannot say that the Dudinka port will be closed," Vetchinin said.
